A reimplementation must therefore treat negative ints as a non-terminating/no-output case rather than printing anything.
    their evidence: timeout 5 ... --f -1 --g 2 -> RC=124, stdout empty, stderr empty. timeout 5 ... --f 1 --g -5 -> RC=124, stdout empty.

content.text: I ran 59 numbered probes. Here are my findings.

verdicts.rule: [1] Byte 0x00 can never be delivered through --c (argv strings are NUL-terminated, bash silently drops it), so 0x00 only ever reaches a bytes value via base58 decoding of --b/--e. This matters only for test-vector generation, not for the repr rule itself.
verdicts.counterexample:
The CONCLUSION holds, but the stated MECHANISM ("bash silently drops it") is wrong for the very quoting route their own evidence used, and it changes expected test-vector values.

Side-by-side, same logical value, only the delivery route differs (P54/P55):
  $ A1=$'AB\x00CD'; A2="$(printf 'AB\000CD')"
  bash: warning: command substitution: ignored null byte in input
  $ /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --a 'T' --b '2' --c "$A1" --d 'y' --e '3' --f 1 --g 2 | sed -n 4p
  b'AB'          <-- ANSI-C quoting TRUNCATES at the NUL
  $ /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --a 'T' --b '2' --c "$A2" --d 'y' --e '3' --f 1 --g 2 | sed -n 4p
  b'ABCD'        <-- command substitution DROPS the NUL, keeps the tail

Leading-NUL case is the sharpest (P55):
  $ B1=$'\x00XYZ'; B2="$(printf '\000XYZ')"
  ... --c "$B1" ... | sed -n 4p  ->  b''      (truncated to EMPTY, not b'XYZ')
  ... --c "$B2" ... | sed -n 4p  ->  b'XYZ'   (dropped)
Anyone generating vectors from "bash drops the NUL" would expect b'XYZ' for $'\x00XYZ' and get b''.

Also not "silent": the command-substitution route prints `bash: warning: command substitution: ignored null byte in input` to stderr. `printf -v CC2 '%b' 'X\0000Y'` also truncates (line 4 = b'X', P49). Mid-string ANSI-C: --c $'AB\x00CD' -> b'AB' (P1); --c $'\x00' -> b'' identical to --c '' (P3/P4).

Their trailing-NUL evidence ($'a\tb\nc\rd\x00') cannot distinguish truncate from drop, which is why the error slipped through.
verdicts.corrected_rule: Byte 0x00 can never be delivered through --c, because execve argv entries are NUL-terminated C strings. Bash's handling of an embedded NUL is ROUTE-DEPENDENT, so pick the route deliberately when generating vectors: (a) ANSI-C quoting $'...\x00...' and printf -v/%b TRUNCATE the value at the first NUL ($'AB\x00CD' -> b'AB'; $'\x00XYZ' -> b''); (b) command substitution "$(printf 'AB\000CD')" DROPS the NUL and keeps the remainder (-> b'ABCD'), and emits a non-silent bash warning to stderr. Either way line 4 never contains 0x00. Verified corollary: 0x00 reaches a printed bytes value only through b58decode of --b (line 2 and line 11, which equals line 2) or --e (line 8) -- lines 1, 3, 7, 10, 12 are pure base58-alphabet output. Verified renderings: --b '1' -> b'\x00'; --e '111' -> b'\x00\x00\x00'; --b '5R' -> b'\x01\x00' (internal NUL); --e '1z' -> b'\x009' (a 0x00 immediately followed by ASCII '9' renders as \x009, with no padding or separator -- a reimplementation must emit exactly two hex digits and must not be confused by the adjacent digit).

verdicts.rule: [2] An invalid-UTF-8 byte in --c does not reach the repr path at all: Python decodes argv with surrogateescape and .encode() raises, producing empty stdout, exit code 1, and a traceback on stderr naming line 17.
verdicts.counterexample:
Survived 12 fresh attack probes; I could not produce a case where an invalid-UTF-8 byte in --c (other args safe) yielded output or a non-1 exit code.

Bad byte at every position, RC=1 / stdout 0 bytes / line 17 in all:
  --c $'\xff'          -> "can't encode character '\udcff' in position 0"  (P11)
  --c $'\x80ABC'       -> position 0                                        (P12)
  --c $'ABC\xfe'       -> position 3                                        (P13)
  --c $'A\xc3'         -> '\udcc3' position 1                               (P15)
  --c $'\xed\xa0\x80'  -> "characters in position 0-2"                      (P14)
  --c $'\xf4\x90\x80\x80' -> "characters in position 0-3"                   (P51)
  --c $'A\xc0\x80Z' (overlong NUL) -> "characters in position 1-2"; no 0x00 sneaks through (P5)
Locale-robust (P21): identical RC=1/line 17 output under LC_ALL=C; LC_ALL=C PYTHONUTF8=0; LC_ALL=C PYTHONUTF8=0 PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0; LC_ALL=en_US.ISO-8859-1 ...; LC_ALL=C.iso88591 ... (only C/C.utf8/POSIX exist on this box).

Sharpenings a reimplementation needs (none contradict the rule as scoped to varying only --c):
1. "line 17" is conditional on --a being encodable and --b decodable. Verified evaluation order, first failure wins: line 15 (--a) < 16 (--b) < 17 (--c) < 21 (--d) < 22 (--e).
   --a $'A\x80Z' --c 'x'        -> line 15 (P16)
   --a $'A\x80Z' --c $'A\x80Z'  -> line 15, NOT 17 (P18)
   --b '0' --c $'A\x80Z'        -> line 16 ValueError: Invalid character '0' (P19)
   --d $'A\x80Z'                -> line 21 (P17)
2. Two message shapes: singular "can't encode character '\udcXX' in position N" for one bad byte; plural "can't encode characters in position N-M" for a RUN of consecutive bad bytes.
3. `position` is a CODE POINT index, not a byte index. --c bytes c3 a9 80 -> "position 1" (not 2) (P50).
4. Only the FIRST bad run is reported: --c $'A\x80B\x81C' -> "'\udc80' in position 1" only (P53).
5. The predicate is "invalid UTF-8", not "non-ASCII": bytes c2 80 are valid U+0080 and succeed, RC=0, line 4 = b'\xc2\x80' (P52). Valid multi-byte input works: 'e' with acute -> b'\xc3\xa9', CJK -> b'\xe4\xb8\xad\xe6\x96\x87', emoji -> b'\xf0\x9f\x98\x80' (P8/P9/P10).
6. The final stderr line is NOT byte-reproducible: the number in `[PYI-NNNNN:ERROR]` is the PID (observed 28210, 33089, 33098, 33764, 55199, 81374, 83030 across runs). Their evidence's 14732 will never recur.

verdicts.rule: [3] Negative --f or --g never reach any print: the process hangs indefinitely (b58encode_int loops forever on negative input) and stdout stays completely empty, so no partial lines are flushed. A reimplementation must therefore treat negative ints as a non-terminating/no-output case rather than printing anything.
verdicts.counterexample:
The "hangs indefinitely" clause and the prescription "treat negative ints as a non-terminating case" are REFUTED as absolutes: a negative int terminates fast with RC=1 whenever an earlier statement raises. All computation (lines 15-26) precedes all prints, and lines 15-18 precede line 19 (--f), while lines 21-22 also precede line 23 (--g).

  $ timeout 10 /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --a 'T' --b '0' --c 'x' --d 'y' --e '3' --f -1 --g 2
  RC=1 (immediate), stdout 0 bytes, stderr:
    File "test20.py", line 16, in <module> ... ValueError: Invalid character '0'      (P31)

  $ timeout 10 /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --a 'T' --b '2' --c $'A\x80Z' --d 'y' --e '3' --f -1 --g 2
  RC=1 (immediate), stdout 0 bytes, stderr: line 17 UnicodeEncodeError                (P30)

  $ timeout 10 /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --a 'T' --b '2' --c 'x' --d 'y' --e 'l' --f 1 --g -1
  RC=1 (immediate), stdout 0 bytes, stderr: line 22 ValueError: Invalid character 'l'  (P32)

A reimplementation that short-circuits on "negative int -> hang" would hang on all three instead of emitting RC=1 plus the correct traceback.

Boundary the rule omits: -0 and -00 parse to int 0 and are NOT negative -- RC=0, full 12 lines, enc_int = b'1', dec_int = 0 (P22/P23/P41). A JS port must not treat -0 as negative (`-0 < 0` is false, so a plain `n < 0` test is already correct; `Math.sign(-0)` is not). Also --f '-1e5' -> RC=2, argparse "error: argument --f: expected one argument" (argparse treats -1e5 as an option token), not a hang (P38).

The no-output half is solidly confirmed: every negative I tried with all other args valid gave RC=124, stdout 0 bytes, stderr 0 bytes -- --f -1, -57, -58, '-001', ' -1', '-1 ', --f=-1, --g -1, --g -5, --g -99999999999999999999, and --f -1 --g -1 together (P24-P27, P33, P39/P40/P42/P43, P57). No partial flush even into a live pipe consumer (P58: `... --f -1 | od -c` prints nothing). Held for a 45 s run: real 45.0s, user 17.7s, sys 27.3s, stdout 0, stderr 0 (P56).

Mechanism partly UNVERIFIED: SIGINT and PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1 + SIGABRT on the PyInstaller worker child both produced no Python traceback, so I could not directly observe b58encode_int as the loop site. Indirect support only: the worker child's RSS grows monotonically (20908 -> 21060 kB over 4 s, P35) with sys-time dominating, consistent with an unboundedly accumulating buffer. Longest observed hang is 45 s; "indefinitely" is extrapolation, not observation.

One disclosure: a single early probe (P24) showed a 78-byte stdout for --f -1. I could not reproduce it in 5 subsequent isolated runs (all 0 bytes), and its line 1 was b'n' = b58encode(b'-'), i.e. as if --a had been '-'. I treat it as a shell/redirect artifact of my own batch harness, NOT program behavior.
verdicts.corrected_rule: Evaluate statements strictly in source order (lines 15,16,17,18,19,21,22,23,24,25,26); the FIRST failure decides the outcome, and because every print is after all computation, stdout is byte-for-byte empty in every failure case. A negative --f hangs (non-terminating, empty stdout AND empty stderr, no partial flush even to a pipe) only if lines 15-18 all succeed; a negative --g hangs only if lines 15-18 and 21-22 all succeed. Otherwise the earlier exception wins and the process exits 1 immediately with that traceback. -0 and -00 are int 0, not negative: they produce normal RC=0 output with enc_int = b'1' and dec_int = 0. Non-int-parsable values like '-1e5' exit 2 with an argparse usage error. Whitespace-padded negatives (' -1', '-1 ') and zero-padded negatives ('-001') do hang, since Python int() strips whitespace and leading zeros.
